The test image shows a mostly green tomato leaf with small, scattered brown spots across the surface. No yellowing halos visible, no webbing, no powdery coating, no mosaic pattern. Spots appear small and punctate.

Top candidates: **Bacterial_Spot**, **Septoria_Leaf_Spot**, **Target_Spot**. Let me view all reference images.
Now let me view the remaining required reference images in parallel:

**Analysis:**

**Test image observations:**
- Mostly green, healthy-looking tomato leaf
- Small, scattered discrete brown/dark spots across the entire leaf surface
- Spots appear uniformly small (pinpoint to 1-2mm), no obvious yellow halos at this scale
- No yellowing, no powdery coating, no webbing, no mosaic/mottling, no large blotches

**Elimination:**
- Early_Blight, Late_Blight: large blotches/concentric lesions with major yellowing — ruled out
- Leaf_Mold, Powdery_Mildew: powdery/pale coating — ruled out
- Mosaic_Virus, Tomato_Mosaic_Virus, Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus: mottling/curling — ruled out
- Verticillium_Wilt: V-shaped lesions, large necrotic areas — ruled out
- Spider_Mites: stippled/bronzed speckling, webbing — ruled out
- Bacterial_Spot: reference shows larger dark lesions often with more yellowing — less consistent

**Key comparison — Septoria_Leaf_Spot vs Target_Spot:**
- The Septoria reference (top-right panel) closely matches: small scattered dark spots on a green leaf
- Septoria description: small (<1/8 in), circular, dark-brown perimeter, on otherwise green leaf — matches well
- Target_Spot: also starts as pinpoint brown spots, but the reference leaves appear even more subtly marked; classic Target Spot progresses to rings, not seen here

The test image is most consistent with early **Septoria_Leaf_Spot** — small, circular, dark-bordered spots distributed across a mostly healthy green leaf surface.
